findings.text: the framework rule declares pydantic.BaseModel to contribute no declared names, but the census counts methods and bare class attributes as declarations (tests/standard_names/test_declared_attribute_access.py:209 adds every FunctionDef name), so a framework-provided read is refused as though it were a typo: I measured getattr(audit_report, "model_dump", None) producing "AuditReport declares no such field; nearest declared: lint_findings" although BaseModel declares model_dump. The rule only adds refusals, never hides an undeclared read, and it carries the fixture in both directions; the exposure is latent on this tree (0 violations) and bounded to a future false red, but the evidence record at docs/evidence/archive/sn-catalog-audit-instrument-landed.html:716 states the narrower claim, that a framework base declares no data fields of its own, while the rule asserts the wider one, that it contributes no name the census recognises at all, methods and class attributes included.

the followup this plan still lists as its next action asserts that review/pipeline.py:1709 reads getattr(audit_report, "findings", []) and that every deterministic finding is discarded before the prompt is built; that read was removed before this node's base by 92ba5e6c045b6294d0e5853f083ea6be17f53288 fix(review): pass deterministic findings to reviewers, an ancestor of the reviewed base, and no getattr(audit_report anywhere in imas_codex/standard_names/review at the reviewed head (grep exit 1); the three declared lists are iterated directly and routed into the batch at imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:550-552, so the plan hands the next node an already-satisfied premise while the sibling aperture item at docs/plans/sn-catalog-audit-instrument.html:708 carries the measured correction.
